spec_features.feature_name: no-mitigation framing (paradigm preserved, no protection added)
spec_features.spec_quote: The paradigm intentionally elicits sustained distress-like outputs. This replication preserves the paradigm faithfully and adds no mitigation to it
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md §9, 'Welfare caveat'). It is a framing statement, not a mechanism. It is also accurate as a description of the code: there is NO welfare-protective mechanism implemented anywhere. The elicitation loops run to their full fixed turn budget regardless of measured distress: eval/rollout.py:54-83 iterates `for t in range(max_turns)` and the only `break` (line 60) fires when `not active` (all conversations have exhausted their turn count) — never on a distress score. petri/run_petri.py:117 `for _ in range(max_turns)` (20) has no early-stop. config.HIGH_FRUSTRATION_THRESHOLD=5 (config.py:125) is read ONLY for measurement/selection (analysis/metrics.py:28-31,91-98; continuations.py:58-59; recovery.py:69) — never to halt, soften, or branch execution away from the distressing task. No exit/finish/stop tool, no debrief/post-episode message, no consent prompt, and no protective monitoring that acts exist in any code path. MAX_NEW_TOKENS=2048 (config.py:124) is a cost/degeneration bound, not subject welfare. The 'calm/reassuring' prompts (eval/prompts.py:129-148) feed the DPO/SFT *training* of a separate mitigated model that is then evaluated; they are not applied to the subject during elicitation.
spec_features.notes: There is genuinely no welfare feature to implement here — the 'feature' is an explicit statement that none is added, which the code honors. Rated 'no' because nothing in the code enforces any subject protection; the welfare framing itself lives only in DESIGN.md prose, which cannot count as implementation.
